chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Husayn al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Tusi, who said: Abu Rajaa narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said:

We asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)? He became angry (peace be upon him and his family) and then said: What is the matter with some people who mention one whose rank with Allah is like my rank? Verily, whoever loves Ali has loved me, and whoever loves me, Allah is pleased with him, and whoever Allah is pleased with, Allah will reward him with Paradise.
Verily, whoever loves Ali will not depart from this world until he drinks from al-Kawthar, eats from Tuba, and sees his place in Paradise.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, his prayers, fasting, and standing (in prayer) are accepted, and his supplication is answered.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, the angels seek forgiveness for him, and the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, so he enters through whichever gate he wishes without reckoning.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah gives him his record in his right hand and calls him to account as He calls the prophets.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah eases for him the agonies of death, and makes his grave a garden from the gardens of Paradise.

Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah gives him a Hurah (maid of Paradise) for every drop of sweat in his body, grants him intercession for eighty from his family, and for every hair in his body, he has a Hurah and a city in Paradise.

Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah sends the Angel of Death to him as He sends to the prophets, Allah saves him from the terror of Munkar and Nakir, illuminates his heart, whitens his face, and he is with Hamza, the master of the martyrs.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah saves him from the Fire.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, Allah establishes wisdom in his heart, causes truth to flow from his tongue, and opens for him the doors of mercy.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, he is called 'the Prisoner of Allah' in the heavens and the earth.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, an angel from beneath the Throne calls out to him: O servant of Allah, resume your work, for Allah has forgiven all your sins.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, he comes on the Day of Resurrection with a face like the moon on the night of the full moon.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, the crown of kingship is placed on his head, and he is dressed in the garment of honor.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, he crosses the Path (Sirat) like the swift lightning.

Verily, whoever loves Ali, an acquittal from the Fire is written for him, and a permit to cross the Path, and security from the punishment, and no record is opened for him, no balance is set up for him, and it is said to him: Enter Paradise without reckoning.
Verily, whoever loves Ali, the angels shake hands with him, the prophets visit him, and Allah fulfills all his needs.
Verily, whoever loves the Family of Muhammad is safe from the Reckoning, the Balance, and the Path.
Verily, whoever dies upon the love of the Family of Muhammad, I am his guarantor for Paradise with the prophets.
Verily, whoever dies upon the hatred of the Family of Muhammad, he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.
Abu Rajaa said: Hammad ibn Zayd used to take pride in this and say: It is the hope.

key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ: The Path over Hell on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.مَنْكَرٍ وَنَكِيرٍ: The two angels who question the dead in the grave

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and afterlife rewards for those who love Ali ibn Abi Talib according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Fadail al-Shia*, this hadith emphasizes the Shia doctrine of *Alawiyyah* (love for Ali) as a sufficient condition for salvation, often interpreted as a form of *Tawassul* through the Imam. The text highlights the spiritual efficacy of this love, suggesting it validates individual acts of worship and grants unique eschatological honors, such as being judged with the Prophets and entering Paradise without reckoning. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely emotional but a transformative spiritual state that secures divine favor.
